claims.text: A predictive approach based on atomic-scale disorder and local vibrational modes will accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The relevant high-entropy alloys have varying compositions.
The relevant high-entropy alloys have varying atomic arrangements.
The predictive model incorporates atomic-scale disorder.
The predictive model incorporates local vibrational modes.
Atomic-scale disorder affects phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Local vibrational modes affect phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
There is a relationship between atomic disorder and phonon transport that can be leveraged predictively.
Leveraging atomic disorder and phonon transport will improve identification of low-thermal-conductivity materials.
The approach will identify high-entropy alloys with lower thermal conductivity than alloys identified by current methods.
The approach will improve prediction accuracy by at least 20%.
Current predictive methods are based on empirical correlations and bulk properties.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys.
The approach may not generalize to other material classes.
The effectiveness of the approach remains uncertain without empirical validation.
Failure to obtain alloys with thermal conductivity at least 20% lower than those associated with current methods will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted improvement is framed as at least 20% greater prediction accuracy, whereas the falsification rule tests whether selected alloys have at least 20% lower thermal conductivity. Prediction accuracy and the conductivity difference between selected materials are distinct quantities, so the benchmark does not directly test the quantified accuracy claim.
